mechanism_sentence 重写（原句为浅述式）。
evidence: Etymonline: "Middle English wilwe, from Old English welig \"willow,\" from Proto-Germanic *wel-..., probably (Watkins) from PIE root *wel- (3) \"to turn, revolve,\" with derivatives referring to curved, enclosing objects. The change in form to -ow (14c.) paralleled that of bellow and fellow."
Etymonline: "Especially a symbol of grief for unrequited love or loss of a mate (1580s); also formerly a wood used to make bats, hence figurative senses in cricket (by 1846)."
willow.mechanism_sentence: willow 是古英语 weliġ——一株枝条柔韧垂弯的树（词根或许与「转、弯」有关，是 Watkins 的推测）：词义千年未变，14 世纪词尾改作 -ow，1580 年代它又成了失恋与丧亲之哀的象征。

semantic_path.how: 守恒的实据在词形与文化层：词形 14 世纪与 bellow、fellow 同步改作 -ow 收尾；1580 年代垂柳在英语文学里成型为哀悼（失恋、丧亲）的象征，柳木作板球棒又带出 1846 年的板球比喻义——树本身的所指从未改变。

changes: original_meaning 保留「葡萄酒」（拉丁语 vīnum/古英语 wīn 的见载义，核对无误）。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明该词的借词性质（日耳曼语早期自拉丁语借入）与现代果酒用法的宽泛化；终极来源两说（Watkins 地中海失传语言说、Beekes 印欧词根说）维持 disputes 登记，路径不裁决。
mechanism_sentence 重写（原句为浅述式）。
evidence: Etymonline: "wine (n.) \"fermented juice of the fruit of the vine, alcoholic drink made from crushed grapes,\" Old English win \"wine,\" from Proto-Germanic *winam, an early borrowing from Latin vinum \"wine\""

Etymonline: "According to Watkins, probably from a lost Mediterranean language word *win-/*woin- \"wine.\" However, Beekes argues that the word is of Indo-European origin, related to Greek itea \"willow,\" Latin vītis \"vine,\" and other words, and that they might derive from the root *wei- \"to turn, bend.\""
Etymonline: "Essentially the same word as vine (q.v.)."
wine.mechanism_sentence: wine 是日耳曼语很早就从拉丁语 vinum 借来的词，与 vine 同源：两千年里它稳稳指着葡萄酿的酒；再往地中海深处追，它的来历有『失传语言』与『印欧词根』两说，至今并立。

semantic_path.how: 借词而守恒：古英语 wīn 自原始日耳曼语的早期借词而来，所指始终是葡萄发酵的酒；现代英语用法上宽泛到其他果酒（词库并列义），但葡萄这一核心从未动摇。

semantic_path 第二站 how 补擦除义的确切年代（约 1900 年，磁记录）与名词湿巾义（1971 年），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "wipe (v.) \"rub or stroke (something) with or as with a soft cloth; rub gently to clear of moisture, dirt, etc.;\" Middle English wipen, from Old English wipian \"to wipe, cleanse,\" from Proto-Germanic *wipjan \"to move back and forth\"..., from PIE root *weip- \"to turn, vacillate, tremble.\" By 1900 as \"to erase\" a magnetic recording."
Etymonline: "wipe (n.) 1640s, \"act or process of wiping...\" 1971 as \"disposable absorbent tissue.\""
wipe.mechanism_sentence: wipe 的老底是「来回地动」（原始日耳曼语 *wipjan 是「往复移动」）：手持布来回抹，是擦拭；1900 年前后，磁头来回一抹、记录全消，也叫 wipe——抹的都是痕迹。

semantic_path.how: 抹的对象换了介质：约 1900 年 wipe 添『擦除（磁带等记录）』义，1971 年名词添『一次性擦拭巾』义——『来回一抹、痕迹全无』的动作画面从桌面一路用到磁头与数据上；词库今义『擦；擦去』统摄两站。

changes: original_meaning 以第一个实词古英语 wyrm 的 gloss 记录为「蛇；龙（泛指爬行之物）」（现行首站用原始日耳曼语的 gloss『虫；蛇』，且漏了龙义，已改）。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年写明所指缩小史（中古泛指爬行有害之物 → 18 世纪科学定型），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "worm (n.) Old English wurm, variant of wyrm \"serpent, snake; dragon; reptile,\" also in later Old English \"earthworm,\" from Proto-Germanic *wurmiz, from PIE *wrmi- \"worm\""

Etymonline: "The word was used through Middle English of any crawling or slithering creature regarded as noxious or dangerous, including serpents, scorpions, maggots... Modern scientific use for a specific Linnaean category of animals is from 18c."
Wiktionary: "doublet of vermin, wyrm, the latter of which is a fairly recent borrowing directly from the Old English"
worm.mechanism_sentence: worm 在古英语里是 wyrm——蛇、龙与一切爬行之物的总称（《贝奥武夫》里的龙就是一条 wyrm）：所指一路缩小，18 世纪科学分类把它定型为不起眼的蠕虫；龙的那一义，如今只活在复古借词 wyrm 里。

semantic_path.how: 所指一路收窄（专化）：古英语晚期 wyrm 已兼指蚯蚓，中古英语里蛇、蝎、蛆等一切被视为有害的爬行之物通称 worm；18 世纪林奈式科学用法把它钉死在无脊椎的蠕虫一类上——词库今义『蠕虫；蚯蚓』即此，巨龙与毒蛇就此退场。
